principle: Map the monetised event before modelling traffic.
comparison: Fresha can earn a fee on an eligible first-client booking. Form3 moves from integration fees to live processing revenue.
conditions: The company discloses a billable event, price mechanism or transition to recurring billing.
exception: One booking or cleared payment may create multiple requests and may use an intermediary.
evidence: Pricing terms, exclusions, integration owner and event denominators.
failure: Multiplying payment value or visits by an assumed infrastructure share.
discovery: Which completed event changes revenue, and how many calls on the path can your team actually influence?

principle: Find the technical boundary of the competitive advantage.
comparison: Ably sells reliable realtime transport. Harmonic sells employee AI security. Oxa sells autonomy where embedded operation and assurance matter.
conditions: The proposed replacement touches the reason customers buy the product.
exception: A separately operated integration, control plane or partner service may still be addressable.
evidence: Customer value proposition, workload allocation and the incumbent design.
failure: Pitching the core product back to its maker.
discovery: Which supporting service would you buy if it released engineers for the part customers pay you to build?

principle: Name the operator, budget owner and beneficiary separately.
comparison: An ElevenLabs developer integration may generate downstream consumption. Oxa deployments can involve several operators and shared responsibilities.
conditions: Customers, partners or private deployments operate a significant part of the production path.
exception: Partner-enabled demand can be commercially valuable without being direct account spend.
evidence: Deployment guide, responsibility boundaries, contract or operating owner.
failure: Attributing all downstream accounts, traffic or devices to the platform vendor.
discovery: Whose account pays for this component when an integration goes live?

principle: Treat a product launch as evidence of a workflow change.
comparison: Research Grid changes the credit analyst's comparison workflow. An Attio interface exposes a permissioned workspace. A MUBI release creates territory-specific eligibility.
conditions: There is a live feature, release note or operator guide with a discernible user action.
exception: A launch can run on an established platform with adequate controls and no new infrastructure decision.
evidence: Release date, interaction path, dependency and observable failure or delay.
failure: Equating an MCP server with inference routing or a release with budget.
discovery: What does the new user action depend on, and which part limits adoption today?

principle: Use hiring to investigate a shared capability.
comparison: A shared platform remit at 9fin suggests a reusable component for several teams. Tessl's actual charging and retention policies give stronger evidence of workload boundaries.
conditions: A dated, employer-specific role describes outcomes and internal consumers.
exception: A role can be filled, cancelled or specify desired background unrelated to production.
evidence: Original vacancy or identified mirror, remit, corroborating product and architecture evidence.
failure: Treating a desired skill as a deployed vendor, open tender or signed budget.
discovery: What do product teams repeat today, and which components have already been chosen?

principle: Ask what incremental value survives the incumbent.
comparison: Attio lists Cloudflare as a subprocessor. Form3's isolation objectives constrain any shared dependency. Harmonic's SIEM handoff is narrower than workforce DLP replacement.
conditions: Existing controls, providers or internal components are documented.
exception: A vendor disclosure rarely identifies exact products, paths or purchased capacity.
evidence: Subprocessor list, integration documentation, resilience design and baseline outcome.
failure: Recommending a greenfield deployment to an existing customer or calling current controls inadequate.
discovery: What would a new component improve against the current control, and what would it make harder?

principle: Separate expansion from permission to serve a workload.
comparison: MUBI must honour territorial rights, voice processing may require regional routing and Oxa partner sites have local control boundaries.
conditions: A proposed cross-region path depends on content rights, residency, contracts or operating authority.
exception: Public assets or synthetic test traffic can have different constraints than restricted production data.
evidence: Region-specific terms, entitlement checks, contract permissions and process owners.
failure: Treating geographic growth as authorization to centralize sensitive workloads.
discovery: Which traffic may cross this boundary and which must remain in the current region?

principle: Distinguish retention, delivery and inference costs.
comparison: Tessl's retention change affects accumulated byte-months. Speech compute and audio transport have different bottlenecks. A model gateway manages compatible requests.
conditions: Fixed commitments, stored data, egress or compute scale with different workload units.
exception: An existing bundled contract, locality rule or model-specific dependency can eliminate savings.
evidence: Retention cohorts, reads, egress, call volume, supported models, current net contract rates.
failure: Inferring model spend or GPU demand from a developer tool, asset or MCP launch.
discovery: Which cost changes when users double or retention extends while daily runs stay flat?

principle: Choose a measurable outcome on the purchasing team's path.
comparison: False positives can block authorised Fresha demand. Faster simulator qualification might bring a bank live sooner. MUBI needs conversion among eligible viewers.
conditions: A technical measurement can be paired with a business event and a relevant control group.
exception: Latency changes might have no impact on completion, certification or renewal.
evidence: Baseline distribution, eligible cohort, owner, control path and success or abort criteria.
failure: Claiming a faster endpoint automatically raises revenue.
discovery: What comparison would show the engineering change caused a business improvement?

principle: Separate growth evidence, initiative readiness and vendor timing.
comparison: A financing announcement, a joint venture and a new security integration each justify different questions. None alone confirms a purchasing decision.
conditions: Evidence dates identify current activity and a plausible stakeholder.
exception: An implementation can already be contracted or an old hiring signal can be stale.
evidence: Dated milestones, named owner, architectural decision window and evidence of evaluation or budget.
failure: Treating investment size as a sales opportunity amount or close date.
discovery: What decision remains open, when will it close and who can still influence it?

principle: Land on a reversible workload and expand only after proof.
comparison: A simulator, a single permissioned interface or a public artwork path can be tested without putting payment clearing, the CRM record or film entitlement at risk.
conditions: A separable pilot has representative traffic, baseline, owner and rollback path.
exception: A nonrepresentative sandbox can hide contractual, availability and volume constraints.
evidence: Pilot acceptance criteria, stop condition and evidence the adjacent team has the same constraint.
failure: Presenting a roadmap of product cross-sells before validating the first workload.
discovery: Which single path would give a decision in one test, and which adjacent path would that evidence cover?

principle: Build explicit stopping conditions into the account decision.
comparison: Core overlap, customer ownership or absent authority can outweigh a strong technical similarity. A well-qualified decision to defer can be the best result.
conditions: No owned commercial gap survives the incumbent, alternatives and ownership checks.
exception: New ownership, a documented service failure or a distinct approved initiative can reopen the question.
evidence: Negative evidence, unknowns and a specific observable reopening condition.
failure: Adding another pillar solely to make the account appear attractive.
discovery: What new evidence would change the decision to defer, and where would it appear?
